gaps: No Korean cuisine at all, despite owning a Big Green Egg and carbon steel wok that are ideal for it.
No Japanese cuisine at all — a whole culinary tradition absent from a household with good equipment.
No North Indian cuisine — the one Indian dish is South Indian; paneer and greens-based curries are completely missing.
Eggs are never used as a protein, leaving a fast, cheap, vegetarian-friendly slot empty.
No Levantine or Middle Eastern mains — the existing 'Middle Eastern-inspired' dish is a stew; the rice-and-lentil tradition is unused.
No Chinese cuisine — the wok's native genre is absent despite the equipment being there.
The weekend project slot is thin: only one true project dish (birria); the Ooni and Big Green Egg can do much more.

ideas.title: Bulgogi (Korean Beef BBQ)
ideas.why: Fills the total absence of Korean cuisine and gives the Big Green Egg its first real BBQ project with a tested, crowd-pleasing marinade.

ideas.title: Mapo Tofu (Vegan Version)
ideas.why: Fills the complete absence of Chinese cuisine and finally puts the carbon steel wok to use in its native genre, as-written for the vegetarian adult.

ideas.title: Saag Paneer
ideas.why: Fills the complete gap in North Indian cuisine and adds paneer as a new protein — a natural complement to the one South Indian dish they already cook.

ideas.title: Mujaddara with Spiced Yogurt
ideas.why: Fills the missing Levantine grain-and-legume tradition and adds lentils as a new protein with a make-ahead dish that improves overnight.

ideas.title: Yotam Ottolenghi's Shakshuka
ideas.why: Fills the egg-as-protein gap entirely and brings a fast, one-pan weeknight dinner from a cuisine and technique the household has never touched.

ideas.title: Japanese Beef Curry (Beef Kare Raisu)
ideas.why: Fills the total absence of Japanese cuisine with a mild, crowd-pleasing Dutch oven project that scales easily to six and tastes better the next day.
